Reading the bar

The bar has three lines. Line 1 is the place you work: the directory, the repository, the branch and the pull request. Line 2 is what the session is doing. Line 3 is what it costs: the model, the context window and the usage limits. Rows for running subagents and git hooks can follow the bar.

Each chip starts with an icon that says what it is about, followed by a number or a short word. The icon carries the meaning, so most chips spend no word on a label: 81% beside the brain is the context window. A label stays only where it says something the icon cannot, such as 5h and 7d, which are window lengths.

Colour tells you how worried to be. A gauge in its normal range has a dark background and a green icon; it turns peach when it is getting close, and red when it is critical or ahead of its pace. Only the highest critical gauge gets a red background, so a red chip is the one to look at first.

When the terminal is too narrow, chips shorten before they disappear, and the least important go first. The context window and the branch are the last to go. A chip with nothing to say is left out instead of drawn empty.

Many chips are links. Clicking the directory opens a terminal there, the branch opens its page on GitHub, the pull request opens the request, the credits open your usage page, and the ? at the right end of line 3 opens this page.

When a figure is missing, old or estimated

  • — means the figure is unknown right now: the source exists but has not answered yet, or its answer is too old to trust.
  • ? in place of a reset means the source sent no reset time, or one the bar cannot believe.
  • off means a feature is switched off on the account, such as extra usage on a seat billed by usage.
  • ~ marks an estimate, such as ~dec 1 00:00 for a reset the source did not send. Everything without a tilde was reported by a source.
  • · 14h after a figure taken from a cache says how old the cache is. Past six hours the chip also loses its colour band.
  • A chip drawn brighter for a few seconds has just changed. A word in bold inside a chip is the item running now.

These chips come from git, from Claude Code's payload, and from gh. The GitHub ones are refreshed in the background and never slow a redraw.

Context window

How full the model's context window is. When it fills up, Claude Code compacts the conversation. · 200k+ in red means the last response's input, cache and output tokens together passed 200,000; · 12m after it says how long the session has been past that point.

Source: Claude Code's payload, sent on every redraw

context

5-hour window

How much of your five-hour usage window is used, and how long until it resets. A mark beside the figure says whether you are ahead of or behind an even pace. +extra means extra usage is on, so work goes on past the limit.

Help

The ? at the right end of line 3 opens this page in your browser.

Source: a file on your disk: a cache the statusline or Claude Code keeps, or your configuration

help

Rows after the bar

Each running subagent gets a row: what it was asked to do, its model and effort, its status when it is not running (queued before it starts), the skills it is using, the step it is on, how full its own context window is, its tokens, how long it has run, and its share of the session's tokens. Finished agents keep their row for two minutes; two or more finished ones collapse into one row such as ✓ 3 done · explore, review.

Each git hook running in one of this repository's worktrees gets a row: which hook, in which worktree and branch, what it is running and for how long, or that it is waiting for another hook's lock.

Switches

Set these as environment variables, for example in your shell profile. The theme and amounts can also go in a .statusline.json file at the root of a repository, as flavor and amounts.

  • CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_LABELS=on puts the words back on the chips whose icon already says them, such as credits 11% and rtk 81% saved.
  • CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_AMOUNTS=hide keeps money and balances off the bar, for when your screen is shared.
  • CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_ACCOUNT chooses the account chip: org (the default), email, tier or off.
  • CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_RESET=clock shows every reset as a time of day in your computer's time zone instead of a countdown.
  • CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_CREDITS_RESET=off drops the estimated reset from the credits chip.
  • CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_SESSION_SHARE=1 adds the session's estimated cost as a share of your monthly cap.
  • CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_MODEL_TIER=1 marks the model +++, ++ or + by price tier.
  • CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_OMIT=help,rtk switches named chips off. help removes the ? that opens this page.
  • CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_ICONS picks the icon set: nerd (needs a Nerd Font), emoji or plain.
  • CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_FLAVOR picks the colour theme, such as mocha, latte, nord or gruvbox.
This page ships with the statusline and opens from your own disk. It loads nothing from the network.
